# Gemba

> The agent-runtime platform. Stand up the environment, run agent sessions,
> read the traces, keep the memory, measure the outcomes, and stop the team
> when it produces more than a human can read. Six commands and five CI
> actions run one loop.

Gemba is the platform a team uses to run coding agents continuously. In Lean
practice, gemba is the factory floor, the place where the work happens. The
loop is stand up, run, see, remember, measure, and stop, and the platform ships
it in two forms: a command family for a terminal and composite actions for
GitHub Actions. What you run in a terminal also runs on every push. Kata is the
reference tenant. It runs this platform every day, and it is a separate product
with its own site at https://www.kata.team/.

Six commands cover the loop. `gemba-harness` runs single-agent and multi-agent
sessions and captures one NDJSON trace. `gemba-trace` queries those traces for
turns, tool calls, errors, and token cost. `gemba-wiki` keeps persistent
memory as boot digests, claims, memos, and integrity audits. `gemba-xmr`
charts a metric as an XmR control chart, so the team acts on real changes
instead of noise. `gemba-benchmark` grades a task family across repeated runs
with hidden tests and reports pass@k. `gemba-watchdog` counts repository
activity over a window and sets an operator latch variable when a counter
breaches its threshold.

Five published composite actions run the same loop in CI. `gemba-bootstrap`
installs the pinned toolchain and the platform CLIs. `gemba-harness` runs an
agent task and uploads the trace. `gemba-wiki` runs a memory command with a
token it mints for the run. `gemba-benchmark` runs benchmark families across
machines and merges the reports. `gemba-watchdog` counts repository activity
and sets the latch on a breach. A workflow pins each action to a commit SHA.

Install the skill pack with `apm install forwardimpact/gemba-skills`, then ask
Claude to stand up the team. For the commands alone, run
`npm install -g @forwardimpact/gemba`.
